s: Good morning team. I'm very proud of all of my new recruits.
You've all gotten past the crawling phase.
You're able to stop people.
You're getting past the walking phase.
You're able to write the invitations.
But now it's time to run.
And how we run is by making solid bookings.

t: Remove the doubt: why before how
s: An important first stop on learning how to make a solid invitation is to remove doubt.
You want to remove doubt in the guest's mind that we're a scam and you want to remove doubt in their minds that we're selling timeshare or promoting water sports and activities.
How we do that is incredibly simple.
You all hear me do it every day, whether it's by giving you my pitch in person or hearing me say it to the guests.
It's right on the pitch map.
The way you remove doubt is giving them the why before the how.
And that comes into place in a lot of places in the inviting process.
First and foremost, if you just run up to people and say, have you been to Eagle Beach yet?
We're promoting Iberostar.
We're going to give you free breakfast and $200.
They're immediately going to think either A, it's a scam, B, it's not true, or C, it's timeshare, let's run away.
So if you tell them why first, it removes the doubt.
Yes, folks, I'm part of the exciting team that's inviting families to the newest hotel on the island to come and take a peek, to have a nice branding experience.
Once you've seen it, hopefully next time you travel, you'll want to stay with us.
I haven't mentioned the club yet, but I also haven't lied to them.
We do want them to see the place.
We do want them to love it.
And we want them to come and stay with us in the future.
Correct? So if you tell them why we are inviting them before we tell them what they get, it removes a lot of doubt and makes the rest of the invitation process go smoother.
Yes, folks, we're inviting as many people as we can to come and see our beautiful hotel.
So next time you travel, you'll consider staying with us.
After you see it, we know you're going to want to stay with us.
And it also helps us spread the word.
You'll tell family and friends about it and maybe take a picture, put it on Facebook, Instagram.
It's all good marketing for us.
And from here, they understand why you're approaching them, what you're inviting them to.
And then you tell them, this is how we do it, or this is how we go.
And from that point, they understand why you're approaching them.
And then when you tell them what we offer, they're more apt to believe it and consider it because it makes sense why you're inviting them.
You've removed the doubt.
After you've told them why we're inviting them, you share with them all the good news.
It's an amazing promotion.
We're actually inviting families for a full branding experience, not just a quick look at the hotel.
When you arrive, we treat you to breakfast at one of our five-star restaurants.
We know you're going to love it.
I see you have a bracelet from Riu.
I'm sure you're eating breakfast at the same place every day.
You're going to love our place.
It's something new, something different for you.
After breakfast, they're going to give you a personalized tour of the property, so you can see for yourself the quality of the facilities and also the service.
And of course, they'll share with you one of our rooms, so you'll be able to anticipate the quality that you'll receive when you stay with us.
And the best part is, we also reward you for your time as a way of saying thanks.
We can offer you $100 in IberoCash that you can use at all the best restaurants and activities, companies on the island, dining and shopping activities.
We work with Gianni's.
We work with Screaming Eagle, Daniel's Steakhouse, just to name a few.
We partner with all the best companies on the island because everybody wants to be associated with Iberostar.
As I told you before, we own the Tierra del Sol golf course and community for three years.
We opened our first hotel a year and a half ago.
We have two more coming.
We have invested a lot in the island and we want to get the word out.
And then you go to the invitation.
You simply say the words, let me get you an invitation.
And that is another good place to start removing doubt, but in this case, from them.

When you say, let me give you an invitation, not would you like one, but let me give you an invitation, they're either going to continue to let you proceed, or they're going to start throwing on you the reasons they don't want to come.
Oh, no, no, no, we already own timeshare.
We can cover that objection.
Oh, no, no, we don't want to be committed to anything.
We can overcome that objection.
Oh, we have things planned tomorrow.
We can overcome that objection.
Really, the only objection that we can't overcome in reality is that they're leaving tomorrow morning.
The rest is all an opportunity to overcome objections.
We won't overcome them all, but we can at least try.

t: 8 o'clock, write it slow, say what it is
s: It's always helpful to say, let me put you down for 8 o'clock, to give them the opportunity to say that's too early.
Then you can offer 10 o'clock.
If they don't say it's too early, you've got a wave-one booking, very easy.
So, once you're writing the invitation, this is your opportunity to slow things down.
There's a tendency to want to hurry through the invitation and get the people moving again because you're getting nervous that they're going to take it or not, that they're going to show up or not.
That is actually when you want to go easy.
Once you're writing the invitation, you've got handcuffs on them.
One family in 100 is going to run away during the invitation writing process.
The rest are going to stay there while you write it.
It's just manners. That's when you slow it down.
Continue making a friend.
Continue doing little discovery questions.
Continue making that bond.
Because if they like you, trust you, and believe you, they will buy from you.
So, that is the best opportunity to solidify a little friendship with them while still doing business.
Once the invitation is written, if it hasn't come up already in the conversation, folks, make sure to bring this invitation with you to confirm which gift you are offered.
And as I told you, when you get there, it's a nice breakfast at one of our restaurants, quick little tour of the property.
And as I mentioned, where we're not selling timeshare, we don't have any weeks or points or maintenance fees, nothing like that.
We're a full-service hotel that you can book direct through travel agents, through Expedia, etc.
But everybody who passes through, we also show you how you can book direct through our loyalty club for preferred rates and cool perks when you travel.
That way you know your options if you do want to stay with us in the future.
To be clear, there's no obligation to be a member to stay there.
We're just like Hyatt, just like Hilton, full-service hotel.
But our members do enjoy significant discounts and really cool perks when they travel.
So if you see something you like in the membership, they'll be happy to show you how to get involved.
If it's not something for you, we still love you anyways because we want you staying at our hotel, whether it's as a member or a regular hotel guest.

t: The phone number: tell them why
s: Phone number is another area where you want to remove the doubt.
Don't just ask for a phone number.
They're going to wonder why.
Are these people going to call us?
They're going to harass us.
They're going to share our information.
If you tell them why when you ask for it, it removes the doubt.
Folks, we also do confirmation calls with our guests.
If you want to give me your phone number, maybe you have WhatsApp on your phone.
That way, one of my managers or supervisors can reach out to you this afternoon between like 5 and 6 o'clock simply to ask you if you're still able to make it.
We're not allowed to solicit or anything like that.
It's just to be able to see if you're still able to make it.
Usually when you explain them why you're asking for the phone number in a very passive, ambiguous way, very comforting way, keep everything simple, they're not going to refuse to give a phone number.
They're not going to wonder why you're asking for a phone number, and they're not going to give a fake phone number.
They want to come. They want that confirmation call.
It makes them feel like VIPs.
So if you tell them why you're asking for the phone number before they ask, you remove the doubt.
Once the invitation is in their hand and the business appears to be done, don't just tell them have a nice day.
Ask them again. So we see you guys tomorrow at 8 for sure?
And if you feel any doubt from the people's response, you're taking their temperature.
If they say something like, oh, we'll try to make it or we'll see, go back again and ask them.
Or, sorry if I misunderstood, but I thought you were pretty sure you were coming.
Well, we don't know this and that and so forth.
Just tell them honestly.
And it's true. It's not a lie.
You know, a lot of families are interested in coming for our open house promotion.
And we certainly wouldn't want to block a space for someone who's sure they want to come if you're not sure you're going to make it.
So tell me, guys, are we going to see you tomorrow at 8?
And they say, yeah, we'll be there.
That's good. You let them understand we're running a business.
This isn't an invitation handing out business.
This is people showing up business.
And if they continue to show doubt, just tell them, you know what, guys, maybe I should give this invitation to somebody else.
I wouldn't want to hold up a space for another family if you're not sure you're going to make it.
That's very important.
There's no shame in getting a solid no.
In fact, it is better to get a solid no than a bunch of fake yeses, where the people tell you, yeah, yeah, we'll be there, and then they don't show up.
Okay. Granted, not every tour shows up no matter what you do.
We all know this. But these are all just little tricks and tips to filter out some of the guests that are just taking your invitation to be friendly and not intending on showing up whatsoever.
And don't be afraid to tell them.
And I tell this to every guest.
I'll be buttoning up a customer for one of our staff.
And I tell them, listen, this nice young man gets a little $65 bonus on his paycheck just for you showing up.
You don't have to book or buy anything.
I know he would greatly appreciate it.
So if you can make it, it's very appreciated.
We'd really appreciate it.
It would mean a lot to him.
You know, let them know it's important to you that they show up.
Your job isn't to just talk to people and hand out invitations.
Your job is to get people to come to the hotel.

And very good when you're reconfirming the agenda at the end to say, and guys, between the breakfast, the property tour, and a little information about the club, we only ask families for 90 minutes, and breakfast tends to eat about half of that.
Never say 45 minutes, never say 30 minutes, never mention any minutes whatsoever, because then they're going to think the presentation is 45 minutes if you do that.
If you just say breakfast tends to eat about half of that, that's very vague and ambiguous.
It makes it sound like the rest of the preview is going to be short and sweet, which it is, by the way.

But the minute you start breaking it down into minutes by saying, oh, breakfast is 45 minutes, property tour is 15 minutes, blah, blah, blah, blah, they think that the presentation is only half an hour, 45 minutes.
And as soon as our hostesses check them in and say, you're aware this is a 90-minute presentation, they say, oh, they told us it's only 45 minutes.
Never mention any minutes.

Folks, like I told you, between the breakfast, the property tour, and a little information on booking direct to the club, we only ask families for 90 minutes, and breakfast tends to eat about half of that, which is not a lie, but it's also very vague.
It's not putting a pin on any specific time.
You've told them 90 minutes.
That's what they need to know.
In this grand total of about 13 minutes of messages, we've covered very important points that will certainly help you increase your show rate.
Listen to these messages.
Listen to them a few times if it helps you.

These are the same things that we say to you at the locations, but for better or for worse, when we're on location, we're usually busy attacking the customers, so we don't always have a chance to discuss these things, especially the PM shift.

But guys, these are all the little sweet tricks and tips that if you listen to them, learn them, start applying them, you'll go from eight bookings a week and one show up to 10 bookings a week and five show ups, six show ups, or more.
Plus, when you give a real expectation why we're inviting them, which is to learn about how they can book direct through our club membership, they go in with that spark of interest.
And when they know they're coming in to be offered something, you have a much greater chance of them buying.
When we just tell them to come check out the hotel and nothing else, then when they find out it's a sales presentation, they're going to be out for the rest of the presentation.
They're going to have their eyes closed and their ears closed.
So if you apply these tips and tricks, if you learn them, if you practice them, you have a better booking rate, better show rate, better Q rate, more tours, more sales.
And it's all a matter of just improving.
Everybody every day in this business can learn more, can improve, myself included, everybody in this business included.
There's always room for improvement.
So please, none of this is criticism to anybody.
It is all just a way to try to help you improve.
It's a good 15 minutes investment to listen to these messages and maybe listen to them more than once or twice.
Thank you all. Have a great day.

If anyone would ever like more tips or tricks or more training, not only can we do it person to person at the location, but we can also set up trainings with myself, with Victor, with Glenn, down at the office on different aspects of the job, not just the basic training we all go through, but we can go through closing training, we can go through covering objections.
We have an awesome team right now.
And I want everybody who's with us right now to grow, to succeed, to make a lot of money, to love their job and to have fun.
So let's do it, guys.
